newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures close up slightly in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures close up slightly in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed slightly higher after a quiet afternoon of mild shortcovering, traders said.
An morning dip to session lows on rate-hike fears was short-lived, with short-covering developing to pull the market back into positive territory, traders said.
"The bias seems to be talk of possible shortcovering, that the market has performed very well on negative news and that at this point the market has held up ok," one Eurodollar desk manager said.
Trade tapered off from midday, with action very quiet late.

"If you look at the last two day's trade it's obvious you had some profit-taking on those short positions and that's basically the tone before payrolls -- squaring up and taking profits," one Treasury bond futures trader said.

March non-farm payrolls were forecast by a Reuters poll of economists to rise 182,000 compared with a 339,000 gain in February. The unemployment rate was expected to edge down to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent in February.
"The market is oversold and people are being very cautious about where they sell it ahead of the report Friday," said Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager for ED and F Man.
"There is a lot of cautiousness right now and I think that we may continue to see that type of trading until Friday," Pullen said.

He pegged support at 107-00 and resistance at 107-24/32 and noted the market stalled out just below that cap. He said the risk was for a challenge of resistance as short-covering continues before the number.
Another floor source pegged support at 107-8/32 and resistance at 108-3/32.
"If we get through 107-8/32 you have to look at 106-22/32 to 25/32," he said.

The early dip this morning was tied to a Washington Post interview with the Fed's Laurence Meyer. He said the economy is "really strong" and "not a fluke." Traders took that to mean a forward-looking Fed will hike rates again.
At the close, June T-bonds were up 3/32 at 107-18/32, notes up 2/32 at 105-24/32, munis rose 8/32 to 112-4/32, Sep bills flat at 94.275, Sept Euros steady at 93.710.
